question: A square field of side 28 m has a circular pond in the center. If the area of the pond is 616 m², what is the area of the remaining field?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of remaining field = Area of Square − Area of Pond

Area of remaining field = (Side)² − 616

Area of remaining field = 28² − 616

Area of remaining field = 784 − 616 = 168 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 168 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square field (a) = 28 m

Area of the circular pond = 616 m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a square = a²

Area of remaining part = Area of square − Area of internal shape

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the square field = 28 × 28

⇒ Area of the square field = 784 m²

⇒ Area of the remaining field = Area of square field − Area of pond

⇒ Area of the remaining field = 784 − 616 = 168 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 168 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Properties

Area = a² | Perimeter = 4a | Diagonal = a√2

Circle Properties

Area = πr² | Circumference = 2πr (where r is the radius)

Largest Circle in a Square

When a circle perfectly fits inside a square of side a, its radius is a/2. It occupies exactly π/4 (approx. 78.5%) of the square's total area.
